chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me:
'O my son! Keep sheep and do not keep camels.'

key_terms.الْإِبِلَ: Camels (collective noun for the camel species)
key_terms.الْغَنَمَ: Sheep (collective noun for small ruminants including goats and sheep)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about keeping sheep versus camels?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advised his son Is'haq to keep sheep rather than camels. This guidance reflects practical wisdom about livestock management: sheep are generally easier to maintain, slaughter, and use for household needs, while camels — though valuable — require more care and resources. In the Islamic agrarian context of early Abbasid Iraq, this represents sound economic advice from a father to a son about the preferred type of livestock for a household.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, 
(It has been narrated) from Is’haq son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me:
‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son! Take the sheep and do not take the camel’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Ishaq ibn Ja‘far who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me,
‘Son, keep sheep but do not keep camels.’”
